papers.title: The social conditioned place preference assay is sensitive to drug dose, training regimen, and social context
papers.abstract: Beginning in the 1960s, researchers have understood that one of the unique properties of psychedelic drugs is that their effects are modified by the context in which they are taken (also known as their set and setting dependence). To date, 7 different studies have shown that critical period reopening is a shared property across psychedelic drugs, including ketamine, MDMA, psilocybin, LSD, and ibogaine. Moreover, the context dependence of psychedelics effects has been recapitulated for both MDMA and ketamine. Recently, Lu et al., Nature Neuroscience 2026 (PMID: 42972049) have claimed that psilocybin does not reopen the social reward learning critical period, which the authors interpret as a failure to replicate previously published results. Here, we re-analyzed results across three published datasets (Nardou et al., Nature 2019; Nardou et al., Nature 2023; Lu et al., Nature Neuroscience 2026) in order to compare the impact of dose, training regimen, and social context on the social conditioned place preference (social CPP) assay. Our analysis reveals that methodological modifications likely account for Lu and colleagues inability to reopen the social reward learning critical period with psilocybin. Nevertheless, because their results recapitulate previous findings that psychedelics effects are context dependent, they support rather than challenge the growing literature demonstrating that psychedelics reopen critical periods.

papers.title: Engineered post-transcriptional regulation of Scn10a by Pumilio ameliorates neuropathic pain in mice
papers.abstract: Post-transcriptional control of mRNA permeates biology, yet its contribution to sensory neuron physiology and pain remains unclear. The mammalian Pumilio proteins PUM1 and PUM2 (collectively referred to as PUM) are RNA-binding proteins that bind Pumilio response elements (PREs), typically situated in 3' untranslated regions. PUM recruits the CCR4-NOT complex to promote mRNA deadenylation and decay. Several mRNAs that encode voltage-gated sodium channels that regulate action potential generation in pain sensing neurons harbor PREs. Here, we explored whether PUM plays a role in pain signaling. PUM1 and PUM2 were enriched in TRPV1-positive dorsal root ganglion neurons, where PUM2 physically interacted with Scn9a, Scn10a, and Scn11a transcripts, which encode Nav1.7, Nav1.8, and Nav1.9, respectively. Depletion of PUM in sensory neurons produced mechanical hypersensitivity and enhanced inflammatory pain. These effects were reversed by blocking Nav1.8 but not Nav1.7, raising the possibility that repression of Scn10a by PUM can be harnessed using synthetic biology to diminish neuropathic pain. To this end, we generated a chimera comprising the RNA-binding domain of PUM2 and a repressive domain, which we dubbed "super-PUM". Expression of AAV-encoded super-PUM in sensory neurons reduced Nav1.8 abundance, diminished tetrodotoxin-resistant and suzetrigine-sensitive sodium currents, and prevented mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity following spared nerve injury. These results demonstrate that optimization of an endogenous post-transcriptional regulon provides a means to ameliorate neuropathic pain.

papers.title: The ANKLE2-VRK1 pathway promotes neuronal resilience by preserving proteostasis during aging
papers.abstract: ANKLE2 is a key regulator of neural stem cell division through inhibition of the kinase VRK1, and mutations in either ANKLE2 or VRK1 cause rare neurodevelopmental disorders that impact brain growth and development. Recent evidence showing that reduced ANKLE2 activity promotes Tau aggregation in vitro suggests that ANKLE2 may also contribute to age-related neurodegenerative processes; however, its role post-development remains unknown. Using Drosophila, we show a novel role for the Ankle2-ballchen (VRK1) pathway in maintaining neuronal resilience and proteostasis. Pan-neuronal and motor neuron reduction of Ankle2 in adult animals shortens lifespan, impairs motor function and accelerates neuronal loss. Lifelong reduction produces more severe phenotypes including an upright wing posture reminiscent of Drosophila Parkinsons disease models. Mechanistically, loss of Ankle2 causes the accumulation of ubiquitinated proteins throughout the central nervous system, indicating impaired protein clearance. Ankle2 mutants have reduced proteasome activity with activation of compensatory degradative pathways, supporting this hypothesis. Loss of Ankle2 behavioral and protein accumulation phenotypes are rescued by expression of human ANKLE2, indicating neuronal ANKLE2 function is conserved between flies and humans. Importantly, VRK1/Ballchen reduction also rescues ubiquitin accumulation and behavior phenotypes caused by loss of Ankle2, demonstrating that the developmental Ankle2-VRK1 pathway is preserved and remains functionally important in aged neurons. More broadly, our findings reveal that a conserved developmental ANKLE2- VRK1 pathway is repurposed in aged neurons to maintain proteostasis and neuronal resilience, providing a mechanistic framework linking neurodevelopmental disease genes to age-associated neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Constrained Geometric Approach for Robust Local Optic Axis Estimation with Single Input Polarization Sensitive Optical Coherence Tomography
papers.abstract: Polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography (PSOCT) enables label-free, depth-resolved microstructure mapping in biological tissues, making it a powerful tool for studying myelinated fiber structures in the brain. Conventional single-input PSOCT measures cumulative retardance and apparent optic axis, which become inaccurate when fibers cross over depth. In single-input PSOCT systems, local optic axis estimation is challenging due to high noise levels, limiting the reliability of depth-resolved orientation estimation. In this work, we present a robust framework for local optic axis estimation in single-input PSOCT that incorporates physical constraints and polarization super-pixels. Polarization super-pixels serve as a preprocessing step to cluster spatially connected pixels with similar polarization states, increasing the effective signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and reducing instability in recursive matrix inversion. In addition, a physical constraint based on the mirror state of the input polarization is enforced during geometric fitting, significantly improving robustness and accuracy under noisy and low-SNR conditions. Experimental validation on ex vivo human brain tissue and phantoms demonstrates substantially improved stability and robustness of local optic axis estimation. This work enables reliable depth-resolved fiber orientation mapping in sophisticated fiber crossing scenarios and extends the potential of single-input PSOCT for analyzing structural connectivity at high depth resolution.

papers.title: The role of shape and local features in human object recognition and learning
papers.abstract: An object's shape is an important visual cue, critical for both perception and cognition. However, the current best models of human vision, Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), do not prioritize shape, but instead, they rely on texture-like local visual features. This raises the question: Could shape be less important for human perception than previously believed? In seven experiments with both adults (N = 300) and 5-year-old children (N = 100), we tested the role of shape and local features in visual object recognition and learning. We found that humans could identify common objects as accurately using local visual features as they could using shape. This finding suggests that, like DNNs, local features may be sufficient for everyday visual recognition and that shape may not be necessary. However, we found that shape played a crucial role in novel object learning, allowing participants to even accomplish one-shot object categorization. Together, these findings force us to reconsider the role of shape in visual recognition and suggest that DNNs, despite not using shape, may nevertheless capture an important aspect of human visual processing.

papers.title: Preserved cognitive control with altered ventromedial prefrontal activity in lichen simplex chronicus: an fMRI study during the Multi-Source Interference Task.
papers.abstract: Lichen simplex chronicus (LSC) is a chronic pruritic skin condition, and one of its central features is the itch-scratch cycle. It has been hypothesized that resisting the urge to scratch, and thereby stopping this cycle, may depend on mechanisms of cognitive control. Here, we used the Multi-Source Interference Task (MSIT) during fMRI to examine whether patients with LSC (n = 9) differ from healthy controls (n = 11) in interference control or in the brain activity that supports it. Our results show that both groups had the expected interference effect, with no statistically significant group differences in behavioral performance or in cingulo-frontal-parietal BOLD activity. Whole-brain analysis revealed a greater interference-related decrease in ventromedial prefrontal cortex activity in patients than in controls. These exploratory findings show distinct patterns of brain activity in LSC while preserving interference control, warranting further investigation in larger samples.

papers.title: Restrictive eating is linked to weaker recollection of food in young adults
papers.abstract: Affective significance often enhances episodic memory, with stronger effects on recollection than on familiarity, but prior research has focused primarily on within-person manipulations of emotional valence. Here, we tested a novel question: whether stable individual differences in the personal significance of food were associated with long-term memory across individuals, given that food ranges from highly appetitive to strongly avoided. Across two experiments, we examined familiarity-based memory (using an image recognition task) and recollection-based memory (using a spatial source recognition task) for food and nonfood stimuli as a function of eating-related individual differences in young adults. In Experiment 1, familiarity-based recognition memory was largely unrelated to eating behavior. In Experiment 2, however, greater restrictive eating and fear of negative consequences from eating were associated with poorer recollection-based memory for food when compared to nonfood stimuli. Together, these findings suggest that individual differences in the affective significance of food do not correlate with episodic memory uniformly but instead are selectively associated with reduced recollection, but not familiarity, of food relative to neutral stimuli.

papers.title: Selective Gut-Related Biomarker Profiles Define Parkinson Disease Trait and State
papers.abstract: Objective: Gut-brain-axis abnormalities are increasingly implicated in Parkinson disease (PD), but most studies examine individual biological compartments of this axis. We asked whether readily accessible stool and plasma-based biomarker profiles show broad or selective gut abnormalities in PD and whether the profiles associated with PD diagnosis (Trait) are the same as those associated with clinical severity (State). Methods: This cross-sectional study included 211 participants with PD and 204 healthy controls. Twenty-four stool and plasma biomarkers were organized into an overall profile, three parent domains (microbiome/dysbiosis, gut barrier/inflammation, systemic inflammation/immune activation), and eight more focused mechanistic profiles. Rank-based Global Statistical Tests (GSTs) compared PD Trait and State. Results: The overall profile showed no evidence of a PD vs. control difference (GST P=0.607; permutation P=0.521), whereas the domain of microbiome/dysbiosis differed (GST P=0.017; permutation P=0.013). Four of eight focused profiles differed nominally: microbial functional-groups, microbial functional-ratios, epithelial injury/bacterial translocation, and myeloid activation. Across PD clinical severity, overall-profile results differed (GST P=0.053; permutation P=0.037); both categories of microbiome/dysbiosis (GST P=0.023; permutation P=0.016) and microbial alpha-diversity (GST P=0.027; permutation P=0.031) differed. Interpretation: The analyses detected differences associated with PD Trait and State in selected gut-related profiles rather than a detectable overall PD-control difference. Microbiome-related profiles showed the most consistent domain findings across PD Trait and State, but they are sufficiently different to suggest that causation and progression of PD follow distinctly different gut processes. These findings refine the concept of the Parkinson gut and prioritize the microbiome for mechanistic and interventional studies.

papers.title: Non-canonical subthalamic nucleus projections regulate motor variability
papers.abstract: Regulation of motor variability is a key hallmark of motor skill learning, balancing motor exploration with optimization of identified task solutions. Nevertheless, the underlying circuit mechanisms in the mammalian brain remain largely unknown. Subnuclei of the dorsal striatum in the basal ganglia promote stereotyped or variable behavior, respectively, and deep brain stimulation of the downstream subthalamic nucleus (STN) can alter motor variability. We therefore tested whether the STN regulates motor variability via non-canonical projections to striatum. We discovered that silencing STN neurons projecting to dorsolateral striatum impaired motor variability reduction in rats developing complex stereotyped movement patterns. In contrast, silencing STN neurons projecting to the anterior thalamic nuclei, or neurons in these nuclei that receive STN input and project to dorsomedial striatum, accelerated variability reduction. These results deepen our anatomical and functional understanding of subcortical motor circuits and reveal unknown roles for STN's non-canonical striatal projections in motor variability regulation.

papers.title: Generalized hippocampal replay exhibits memory recall-like dynamics
papers.abstract: Hippocampal replay has been intensely studied for theorized roles in memory consolidation, credit assignment in reinforcement learning, and online planning. Much work in the field assumes that replayed trajectories traverse states smoothly and sequentially, in either forward or reverse order of experience. In a synthetic setting, we demonstrate that incorrect transition priors lead to systematic decoding error and show how model comparison addresses this issue. We compare a diverse set of transition models, including recall-like transition dynamics, and show how they can capture qualitatively different replay structures. Applying model comparison to three neural recording datasets from adult male rats, we find that the recall transition dynamics offer a statistically superior description of spiking during population burst events compared to a commonly used heuristic model of smooth trajectories. We propose a generalized conception of replay events through this theoretical connection to human free recall dynamics. Furthermore, our theory suggests that generalized replays may be a neural instantiation of online planning through generalized rollouts. We find preliminary evidence that generalized replays are more prevalent in settings where planning is beneficial. Overall, the proposed theory has implications for decoding methodology and the normative interpretation of hippocampal replay.

papers.title: "The self" as shifting coalitions of brain systems in a continuous configuration space
papers.abstract: Philosophers and psychologists distinguish many forms of self, yet neuroimaging results often implicate a shared core in the cortical midline or insula. We propose self-related processing arises from shifting coalitions of distributed brain systems, without a core. In a meta-analysis of 912 neuroimaging publications, titles and abstracts clustered into ten forms, including autobiographical memory, body ownership and interoception. No single location was significant in all ten associated brain maps, although each occupied different parts and amounts of midline and insular territory. Their differences were distributed across the brain. Regional patterns varied with study context, corresponded selectively with aspects of consciousness and resembled maps of general functions. Brain patterns combined at continuously varying strengths predicted regions reported in held-out publications better than single patterns or on/off combinations. Self-related processing therefore has no core and arises from shifting coalitions of distributed brain systems whose graded contributions define a continuous configuration space.

papers.title: Restoring Marcenko-Pastur noise estimation and denoising of diffusion MRI under common image reconstruction
papers.abstract: Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging can reveal microstructure in the living brain, but the measurements are inherently noisy. Marcenko-Pastur denoising is a widely used remedy, helping to separate signal from noise under a simplified noise covariance model. However, we find that the model breaks under common image reconstructions across 28 public in vivo datasets, resulting in weaker denoising than intended. We restore the intended denoising behavior with a noise covariance model estimated from the reconstructed images, and validate the estimated model on repeated ex vivo and in vivo scans. The method requires no additional measurements or knowledge of the reconstruction, opening headroom for microstructure analyses in both existing and newly acquired data.

papers.title: Scalable construction of near-wild-type brain atlases enables variability-aware neuronal identification in C. elegans
papers.abstract: Matching cells across individuals is essential for comparing cellular data but becomes challenging when cell positions vary between animals. Here we introduce a framework for constructing probabilistic neuronal atlases by integrating partially overlapping observations from sparsely labeled, near-wild-type strains to reconstruct cellular organization from incomplete observations. Using five strains imaged without compression in a microfluidic array, we built an atlas of 129 head neurons (55 classes) that captures positional variability and infers spatial relationships even between neurons never observed together. We find that variability is spatially structured with neurons in compact regions being more stereotyped, while neuronal relative positions are more stable than their absolute positions. Exploiting these statistical relationships, variability-weighted identification improved top-1 accuracy to 86.3%, approaching human inter-annotator agreement, with the correct identity among the top three candidates in 98.2% of cases. Relationships stitched across strains reproduced observations in a held-out strain, and the atlas supplied correct identities in males and in pan-neuronal calcium imaging in vast majority of cases. Our extensible framework enables community-built atlases and offers a strategy for cell identification when anatomical variability limits template-based registration.

papers.title: Hormone therapy attenuates menopause-related impairments in motor cortical spike-timing-dependent plasticity
papers.abstract: The menopause marks the permanent cessation of menstruation via a decline in endogenous hormone production. This transition influences brain health, yet its effects on motor cortical excitability and spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) are poorly understood. Across two sites, 46 females were categorised as pre-menopausal (PRE, age 28{+/-}7 years), perimenopausal (PERI, 50{+/-}3 years), post-menopausal (POST, 60{+/-}8 years), or combined continuous hormone therapy users (HT, 52{+/-}3 years). Transcranial magnetic stimulation was used to measure corticospinal excitability (MEP/Mmax), short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI), and intracortical facilitation (ICF) before, then 10 and 30 min after a paired associative stimulation (PAS) protocol (25-ms interstimulus interval). Serum hormone concentrations were quantified from venous blood. Resting corticospinal excitability and SICI were not different between groups before the PAS protocol. However, a group x time interaction (p=0.0152) for MEP/Mmax revealed distinct STDP responses. PRE showed a significant increase in corticospinal excitability following PAS (+48%, p=0.0045), whereas PERI and POST showed no facilitation (p[≥]0.2079). Between groups, both PRE and HT exceeded PERI, and HT also exceeded POST; however, HT users showed a smaller, non-significant increase (+32%, p=0.0666) that collectively distinguished them from the blunted responses of PERI and POST. The magnitude of STDP was not associated with any single hormone or chronological age across the whole sample of participants. These findings provide the first evidence that motor cortical STDP is influenced by menopause stage. With blunted responses in PERI and POST, yet preserved responses in HT users, these data have implications for motor learning and rehabilitation across the female adult lifespan.

papers.title: Distal inhibition is recruited for action but not sensation in the primate superior colliculus
papers.abstract: Sensorimotor transformation requires neural circuits to coordinate excitation and inhibition, but how and whether this organization changes as the circuit transitions from processing sensation to action remain unresolved. We recorded laminar local field potentials across superior colliculus (SC) layers in four male macaques and computed current source density to resolve transmembrane currents during saccades to a target at one of eight isoradial directions. During the visual response, excitation was spatially confined to the receptive field, with little modulation at distant sites. During saccade generation, local excitation remained strongest for movements toward the receptive field, while inhibition extended across the SC map, including locations where spiking remained at baseline. Because the same recordings detected distal inhibition during movement, its absence during vision cannot reflect insufficient sensitivity, indicating that distal inhibition is selectively recruited during action. After saccade completion, excitation emerged regardless of saccade direction, potentially reflecting a rebound from, or release of, the preceding inhibition. These patterns were only partly reflected in spiking activity, which primarily captured local excitation, unmasking circuit dynamics largely invisible at the level of neuronal output. Together, our findings reveal a striking reconfiguration of SC population dynamics across sensorimotor transformation, spanning from spatially restricted excitation during sensation, to local excitation coupled with distal inhibition during movement generation, then to global post-movement excitation. Thus, fixed circuit architecture can express a sequence of behaviorally gated excitation-inhibition states largely invisible to spiking output.

papers.title: Partially shared representational space for vision and language across objects, scenes, and visual events
papers.abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) and behavioural similarity judgements of visual stimuli predict neural responses in visual cortex. Recent work shows that large language model (LLM) embeddings and similarity judgements of language descriptions also predict visual brain activity. These predictors were examined separately across modalities (vision vs language) and types (models vs human behaviour). It remains unclear to what extent these predictors explain shared or unique aspects of visual brain responses, how these contributions vary along the visual hierarchy and category-selective regions, and whether vision-language convergence depends on the stimulus type. We used three fMRI datasets progressing toward naturalistic visual experience, from objects (THINGS) to scenes (NSD) to dynamic events (BMD). For each dataset, we collected similarity judgements of visual stimuli and of their language descriptions from human participants (N = 21-35), extracted vision DNN features and LLM embeddings, and related similarity judgements and model representations to visual brain responses using representational similarity analysis (RSA) and variance partitioning. Vision-language convergence was higher within behaviour than within models. From objects to dynamic events, LLM alignment with vision-based similarity judgements increased, whereas vision DNN alignment remained stable. A shared, predominantly cross-modal component increased along the visual hierarchy and dominated explained variance in high-level visual cortex. LLMs made their largest unique contributions in face- and body-selective regions (FFA and EBA), where shared representations of vision- and language-based human similarity judgements also explained variance beyond the models. In summary, we find a partially shared representational space for vision and language in high-level visual cortex, most clearly in regions representing social information related to people and their actions. As each predictor retained unique variance, combining computational models and human behaviour across vision and language may offer a more comprehensive account of high-level visual representations.

papers.title: Early visual experience contributes to the calibration of higher-order body representations
papers.abstract: Higher-order body representations, including representations of body shape and size, play an important role in maintaining perceptual constancy in touch. However, whether the development of these representations depends on early visual experience remains unclear. Here, we investigated tactile distance perception in congenitally blind, late-blind, and sighted individuals. A given tactile distance is typically perceived as longer on the finger than on the forearm, reflecting distortions in cortical topography that is partially rescaled by higher-order representations of body size and shape. Congenitally blind participants showed a greater tendency to perceive identical tactile distances on the index finger as longer than those on the forearm. A similar bias was observed when comparing the forehead and face, suggesting that altered tactile distance perception in congenital blindness is not limited to body regions with extensive sensory-motor experience. Furthermore, within the late-blind group, the similarity of perceptual patterns to sighted controls, relative to congenitally blind participants, was associated with blindness duration. Together, these findings suggest that both early visual and post-blindness experience contributes to the calibration of tactile distance perception across the body, with its influence potentially extending beyond body regions extensively engaged in sensory-motor activities.

papers.title: Variable penetrance of schizophrenia in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome is associated with impaired, but reversible, neuronal mitophagy.
papers.abstract: The 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22qDS) is a major genetic risk factor for schizophrenia (Sz). We found that iPSC-derived neurons (iNeurons) from 22qDS +Sz individuals exhibit weaker mitochondrial energetics, whereas iNeurons from individuals with the same deletion but no psychosis (22qDS -Sz) upregulate expression of mitochondrial biogenesis-related genes. Here, we investigated why the +Sz group fails to undergo this compensation, finding that 22qDS +Sz iNeurons have older and more depolarized mitochondria than 22qDS -Sz or controls. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed downregulation of mitophagy-related pathways, and live imaging revealed elevated lysosomal pH. Restoring lysosomal acidity with acidifying nanoparticles improved mitophagy and, remarkably, increased the expression of mitochondrial biogenesis-related transcription factors in the +Sz neurons. We conclude that lysosomal dysfunction and impaired mitophagy differentiate 22qDS individuals who develop schizophrenia from those who do not. Mitophagy could be a novel therapeutic or preventative opportunity for Sz in the context of genetic neurodevelopmental disorders.

papers.title: Cerebellar transcranial AC stimulation produces frequency and phase-dependent changes in Purkinje cell complex spike waveform
papers.abstract: Cerebellar transcranial alternating current stimulation (ctACS) can improve motor learning and may speed rehabilitation. The mechanisms by which ctACS induces long-term changes in brain function that underlie these effects are not known, and knowledge of them could greatly improve the application of ctACS. One potential mechanism is alteration of Purkinje cell (PC) complex spike (CS) activity, as CS activity is a key regulator of cerebellar synaptic plasticity. Thus, we investigated how ctACS modifies CS firing rates and waveform. Extracellular recordings were obtained from cerebellar PCs in anesthetized adult rats while ctACS (250 A) was applied across a range of frequencies (0.5 - 50 Hz). The effect of ctACS on CS waveform was quantified via measuring changes in the overall size of the CS and in the number and amplitude of the spikelets that comprise a CS. ctACS produced phase-dependent modulation of the CS waveform in a majority of PCs at most tested frequencies, with 1 Hz stimulation causing modulation in all PCs tested at the frequency. The modulation reflected changes within the normal range of CS waveforms rather than an expansion of that range. Analysis of individual spikelet periods (windows) revealed that ctACS modified discrete portions of the CS, with 93.8% of PCs showing significant modulation in at least one window. Notably, the strength of phase-dependent CS waveform modulation was relatively consistent across frequencies, in contrast to the frequency dependence of simple spike (SS) entrainment. Significant modulation of spikelet amplitude was found more often than that of spikelet number; however, the relative strength of the modulation when present was similar for the two parameters. CS waveform modulation was correlated with SS entrainment strength and was strongest in PCs located near the cerebellar surface (i.e., near the apices of the folia). Together, these findings demonstrate that ctACS exerts phase-dependent control over CS waveform. Moreover, the differing frequency dependence of the waveform effects and SS firing modulation suggests that it may be possible to target CS-related plasticity selectively, providing a potential strategy for selectively modulating cerebellar learning with ctACS.

papers.title: EPHB2 promotes long-range axon extension and its variants cause callosal dysgenesis
papers.abstract: The corpus callosum (CC) is the largest fibre tract connecting the cerebral hemispheres, essential for integrating neural activity across large-scale brain networks. Accordingly, abnormal CC development is associated with diverse neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders. Callosal projection neurons (CPNs) of the cortex form the CC by extending long-range axons to the contralateral hemisphere; however, the mechanisms that sustain axon elongation over such remarkable distances remain poorly understood. Here we show that variants in the human gene EPHB2, which encodes a tyrosine kinase receptor regulating nervous system development and implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders, cause CC dysgenesis. We characterise variant- specific effects on EPHB2 signalling and demonstrate that variants identified in individuals with distinct CC morphologies differentially alter CPN axon outgrowth and integration in vivo. We further show that EphB2 has a cell-autonomous, ligand-independent function in promoting CPN axon outgrowth by spatially organising actomyosin at axonal growth cones. These findings reveal a previously unrecognised role for EphB2 in promoting long-range axon extension and provide the first evidence that EPHB2 variants cause CC dysgenesis in humans. More broadly, our study links molecular variation in EPHB2 to individualised abnormalities in brain connectivity and provides a framework for understanding how heterogeneous circuit-level phenotypes arise in neurodevelopmental disorders.

papers.title: E2F4 gene therapy reverses established synaptic and cognitive deficits and remodels learning-associated signaling in Alzheimer's disease mice
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) causes progressive synaptic dysfunction, neurodegeneration, and cognitive decline, yet strategies capable of reversing established deficits remain limited. Here, we show that neuronal expression of a p38MAPK phosphorylation-resistant human E2F4 variant (hE2F4DN), delivered by adeno-associated virus, restores hippocampal long-term potentiation and memory in homozygous 5xFAD mice after functional impairment is established. Treatment also reduces amyloid-{beta} and phospho-tau pathology and prevents hippocampal neuronal loss. Integrated proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses reveal remodeling of metabolic, redox, neuroimmune, synaptic-vesicle, and GSK3{beta}-associated signaling pathways. Following contextual fear conditioning, hE2F4DN-treated mice exhibit broader learning-associated synaptic proteomic signatures and distinct phosphoregulatory responses involving synaptic machinery. These findings demonstrate that E2F4 gene therapy can reverse established synaptic and cognitive deficits while preserving neuronal integrity and reshaping molecular responses to learning, identifying E2F4 phosphorylation as a potential therapeutic target for advanced AD states.

papers.title: Complex Spatial and Temporal Organization of Functional Brain Networks
papers.abstract: Recent research exploring brain-behavior associations has relied on the language of complex systems to understand how stable behavioral individual differences emerge from brain function. At the same time, advances in neuroimaging have provided greater insight into both the topological and temporal properties of macroscale cortical networks. These new approaches offer a potential avenue for understanding how functional activity in the brain might behave in a manner that aligns with complex-systems interpretations of psychological traits. The present study used resting-state data from the Human Connectome project (N = 994) to explore associations between the spatial and temporal features of functional brain networks. Using an adaptive frequency approach to explore brain function at different timescales together with a family of methods from complex systems theory, we identified patterns of brain state organization reflecting a state-trait continuum, with more stable trait-like dynamics and greater functional coupling between networks in lower frequency oscillations. Additionally, we found evidence of greater coupling across timescales in brain networks associated with higher-order cognition. This research supports interpretations of brain organization as a spatiotemporal hierarchy and provides future avenues for exploring brain-behavior associations from a complex system perspective.

papers.title: Microglial Stim1/Stim2 deletion reduces calcium signaling but promotes infarct expansion after ischemic stroke
papers.abstract: Microglia respond to ischemic stroke with calcium transients carried by calcium release-activated calcium (CRAC) channels, gated by the endoplasmic reticulum sensors Stim1 and Stim2. Since CRAC signaling drives pro-inflammatory responses in immune cells, blocking it in microglia should protect the ischemic brain. We have examined this hypothesis in 15-month-old mice lacking Stim1 and Stim2 in microglia (Cx3cr1-CreERT2; Stim cKO). In vivo two-photon imaging confirmed that cKO microglia produced one-third smaller calcium transients during cortical spreading depolarizations. We then followed distal middle cerebral artery occlusion (dMCAo) with multiparametric MRI at 9.4 T. Six hours after occlusion, both the control and cKO genotypes demonstrated similar infarct size, edema, and diffusion, but lesion perfusion tended to be lower in cKO mice. Differences in tissue injury emerged later. Between 6 and 48 hours, the infarcts in control males did not grow, whereas infarcts in cKO males expanded 2.7-fold. At 48 hours, cKO males had 2.2-fold larger infarcts, while cKO females did not differ from controls. Moreover, cKO lesions showed a lower apparent diffusion coefficient, indicating more severe tissue injury. Neither hemispheric swelling nor cerebral arterial anatomy accounted for these differences. Contrary to our hypothesis, ablating microglial CRAC channels worsened stroke outcome. Microglial CRAC signaling may therefore protect threatened tissue in the first days after ischemia, possibly by sustaining its perfusion, and this role appears to outweigh its pro-inflammatory effects.

papers.title: Inactivation of tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase reduces phosphatidylcholine amounts in the brain of infant mice
papers.abstract: Hypophosphatasia is a rare disease caused by dysfunctions of tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase (TNAP). TNAP is expressed in numerous tissues, notably the brain, and patients with hypophosphatasia exhibit neurological symptoms, including epilepsy in the most severe forms of the disease. TNAP knockout (KO) mouse models have provided a wealth of information regarding TNAP functions. Specifically, metabolomic studies focusing on the aqueous fraction of the brain of TNAP KO mice identified numerous molecules whose amounts were altered as a direct or indirect consequence of TNAP inactivation. Among these molecules, several are involved either directly (e.g., vitamin B6) or indirectly (e.g., N-acetylaspartate) in lipid metabolism. In this study, we therefore extended these investigations by examining the consequences of TNAP inactivation on the brain lipidome. We used a targeted lipidomic approach, examining four main categories of lipids: fatty acids, neutral lipids, sphingolipids and glycerophospholipids, subdivided into 16 lipid classes and amounting to 296 lipid species. Eleven lipid species showed significantly reduced amounts in the brain of TNAP KO mice. All belonged to the phosphatidylcholine class. As phosphatidylcholines are major constituents of brain cell membranes, our results suggest that hypophosphatasia could be associated with alterations in membrane structure and functions, which could contribute to the neurodevelopmental disorders associated with the disease.

papers.title: Nucleus reuniens gates selective hippocampal-prefrontal interactions during NREM sleep
papers.abstract: Memory consolidation requires functional synchrony between the hippocampus (HC) and the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC). The nucleus reuniens (RE) is a structural and functional hub between HC and mPFC. Here, we used in vivo electrophysiology to monitor the hippocampal-thalamic-prefrontal network in rats during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep. We identified ripple-like activity in the RE (120 Hz peak frequency, 45 ms oscillatory duration) that occurred most frequently during NREM sleep and was associated with robust recruitment of thalamic neural spiking. RE ripple activity was phase-locked to both hippocampal sharp wave-ripples (SWR) and mPFC ripples. Although ripples were independently detected in all three structures, we found that coupling between HC and mPFC ripples mainly involved co-occurring RE ripples. These results suggest RE ripples help organize when hippocampal activity engages prefrontal circuits during sleep, with potential implications for network mechanisms of memory consolidation.

papers.title: Repeated self-administered EEG recordings enable longitudinal measurement of brain activity at home
papers.abstract: Mobile electroencephalography (EEG) offers new opportunities to investigate brain activity outside the laboratory, but the quality and reliability of self-administered recordings remain important concerns. Here, we evaluated whether repeated at-home recordings using a four-channel consumer EEG device could provide meaningful electrophysiological measurements and characterized the stability of these measures across sessions. Five participants completed repeated recordings across multiple days, including resting-state measurements and an auditory oddball task performed with and without concurrent cognitive load. The recordings captured established spectral signatures of physiological state and task demands, including increased alpha activity during eye closure and changes in theta activity associated with cognitive load. Auditory stimulation elicited clear event-related responses, while exploratory multivariate decoding distinguished standard from target tones across recording sessions. Measurement stability varied across electrophysiological features, and aggregating repeated sessions improved the consistency of individual-level estimates. For example, split-half reliability of the auditory N1-like response increased from r = .22 with one session to r = .76 with seven sessions per half. By demonstrating the feasibility of repeated self-administered EEG measurements, this study provides a step toward investigating how brain activity varies both between individuals and within individuals over time in everyday environments.

papers.title: Electrophysiology of multisite direct electrical stimulation in the human brain
papers.abstract: Human cognition and neurological disorders reflect properties of distributed networks, yet how best to engage these networks therapeutically remains unknown. Multisite stimulation is a principled strategy for engaging brain networks, but a key translational barrier is understanding how a network combines concurrent inputs from multiple nodes. Here, we investigated the electrophysiology of simultaneous multisite direct electrical stimulation in 20 participants implanted with stereo-EEG electrodes. Synchronized dual-site stimulation engaged a larger effective network than single-site stimulation. Linear superposition explained most responses, but distinct nonlinear responses were also observed. Sublinear responses, consistent with saturation, occurred proximal to stimulation sites, while supralinear responses arose in network-connected sites during the response's late component. Moreover, low-intensity dual-site stimulation matched or exceeded single-site stimulation at higher intensities. These principles extended to three-site stimulation. These findings systematically characterize how responses to simultaneous multisite stimulation interact in the human brain, a foundational step towards principled, network-guided neurostimulation therapies.

papers.title: Amyloidosis and tauopathy progressively disrupt near-critical dynamics in selectively vulnerable circuits
papers.abstract: Mechanistically distinct neurodegenerative diseases result in similar cognitive deficits, and pathology is often concentrated in a set of circuits known to be selectively vulnerable. Selective vulnerability is an intrinsic property of a circuit: in APP/PS1 mice, where plaques are global, functional disruptions are confined to circuits within the default mode network. What characterizes the dynamics of vulnerable circuits from those of spared circuits is unknown. We asked whether the distinguishing property is the proximity of population dynamics to criticality, a homeostatic set-point of network activity that determines computational capacity. We recorded single units simultaneously in three selectively vulnerable regions (retrosplenial cortex, anterior cingulate cortex, and CA1 hippocampus) and in primary visual cortex of freely behaving young and old APP/PS1 and wild-type mice. Firing rate and spike-time variability differed by genotype inconsistently across regions and ages. In contrast, three measures from criticality theory each revealed deficits that emerged only with age and only in the vulnerable regions. No measure detected a progressive change in V1. Avalanche scaling is not fixed in neural activity, but varies along a scaling line as the network state changes. As a result, the lines generated by each genotype revealed a constitutive effect of the transgene in young animals, which inverted with age in amyloid-bearing animals, but only in vulnerable circuits. If the destabilization of near-critical dynamics directly reflects a circuit's functional capacity, the same signature should identify a mechanistically distinct degenerative disease. In a model of tauopathy (P301S/E4), CA1 dynamics were displaced from the control scaling line with the same age-dependent reversal observed in APP/PS1. Our results suggest a network-level principle of neurodegenerative diseases: molecularly unrelated pathologies converge on the loss of near-critical dynamics in selectively vulnerable circuits.

papers.title: Satellite glial translatome reprograms to favor mitochondrial and vesicular signaling under pelvic pain conditions
papers.abstract: Sensory satellite glial cells actively contribute to inflammatory and neuropathic pain, but their roles in pelvic pain remain unclear. This study examined how the active translating mRNAs in sensory SGCs change during pelvic pain symptoms using translating ribosome affinity purification followed by RNA sequencing (TRAP-seq) in a chronic pelvic pain (CPP) mouse model. Our data showed that SGCs exhibit sex-specific translatome patterns at baseline, which were reprogrammed in CPP conditions under the control of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4E (Eif4e). In CPP conditions, sensory SGCs exhibit increased translation of mitochondrial and vesicular genes and suppression of immune genes in both sexes; an anti-inflammatory cytokine profile was detected in female pelvic sensory ganglia. We are the first to characterize SGC translatome in pelvic pain conditions and to report sex differences in SGC translatome. Our data suggested that mitochondrial and vesicular gene translation in sensory SGCs may be important to afferent hypersensitivity.

papers.title: A Variational Principle for the Emergence of Neural Geometry Underlying Bayesian-Like Behavior
papers.abstract: Neural population geometry constrains how task variables are represented and read out into behavior. We propose a variational principle in which learning balances task accuracy and representational smoothness under stimulus-dependent weighting. This balance links stimulus statistics to the shape of a latent neural coordinate. For magnitude estimation, the principle predicts distortions near the edges of bounded ensembles, global affine contraction for Gaussian ensembles, and warping toward high-probability regions for bimodal ensembles. We test the bounded-uniform case in recurrent neural networks trained to reproduce time intervals. Their learned geometries occupy three regimes as the boundary distortions change from too narrow to resolve, to measurable, to extending across the stimulus range. A shape parameter selected from an empirical neural coordinate predicts the nonlinear component of mean behavior through an affine readout, with only behavioral gain and offset fitted afterward. In this bounded-uniform setting, the variational coordinate and Bayesian least-squares mean response have closely matching shapes after affine normalization. These results suggest a variational account of how stimulus statistics shape neural geometry and yield Bayesian-like behavior.
